summary: Decision (owner fdev, FS-GG/FS.GG.Game#727): the profile policy deadline (250 ms) bounds guest policy work only. A load still creates the module Worker and posts its command at once; the Worker's first Compile receipt for that command is its readiness report. Before readiness the control is projected in phase 'start' under a separate startup bound (HostSettings default 5000 ms, selectable 1-60000 ms, capped by any caller enclosing deadline); expiry there is the distinct appended DeliveryReason.WorkerStartTimeout (Discarded, TimedOut/Compile, not dispatched, Worker terminated, no game authority). Readiness replaces the startup timer with the policy timer; compile/other receipts before readiness, repeated readiness and readiness after expiry are inert; ready-Worker requests keep enqueue budgets. The canonical lifecycle model, schedules (default 58/selected 16), F# correspondence and unit tests agree; coherent source version 0.7.0, ApiCompat-compatible with published 0.6.0. Lesson: Firefox reduced timer precision lets setTimeout callbacks observe floor(performance.now()) <= due (measured 36/300; Chromium/WebKit 0/300). A connected-interpreter timer observation that expires nothing was never re-armed, so a looping guest could hang unretired (intermittent 15 s Firefox watchdog hangs); the interpreter now delivers timer observations only after the clock passes due and re-arms the remainder. Lesson: WebKit words wasm traps 'Unreachable code ...'; compare trap diagnostics case-insensitively. Sampling: requiring an explicit readiness step made the selected frozen-commit-expiry witness (a 1-in-1000 lucky sample on main, 0 at four other seeds) unreachable; an initialized-candidate sampled entry makes it structurally reachable (14/1000) instead of changing the pinned seed. Local evidence only at capture: 20 fresh-profile cold loads per browser pinned to 4 CPUs in Ubuntu 24.04 measured startup max Chromium 16 ms, Firefox 46 ms, WebKit 24 ms and policy load max 2-4 ms. Hosted cold-load evidence, publication, Templates re-pin and installed acceptance are separate later boundaries.
title: Worker startup is bounded separately from the WASM policy deadline; Firefox timers can fire before due
